title: Collapse Sorted Numbers into Ranges
statement:
You get a strictly increasing array of integers nums, like the selected page numbers in a print dialog. Describe it as a list of ranges, the way "pages 1–4, 7, 9–10" reads.

Group numbers that follow each other with no gap (each one exactly 1 more than the previous) into one range. Write a range of several numbers as "a..b" and a range of one number as just "a". Return the ranges from smallest to largest.

Every number must be covered, and no number that isn't in nums may be covered. Use as few ranges as possible.

examples.why: 5 has gaps on both sides, so it stands alone.
Negative numbers work the same way: −1, 0, 1 are consecutive.

hints: A range ends exactly where the next number is not one more than the current one.
Keep the index where the current range started. Walk forward until the run of +1 steps breaks.
When the run ends at j, emit nums[start] alone if start == j, else nums[start]..nums[j]. Then start the next range at j + 1.

explain.intuition: Because the array is sorted with no repeats, a range is just a maximal run where each step is exactly +1. Two pointers find each run: i marks where a run starts and j walks forward while nums[j + 1] == nums[j] + 1. When the run stops, write it out and start the next one at j + 1. Every index is visited once.
steps: Set i = 0 and an empty output list.
While i < n: set j = i and move j forward while j + 1 < n and nums[j + 1] == nums[j] + 1.
If i == j, push String(nums[i]); otherwise push nums[i] + ".." + nums[j].
Set i = j + 1 and repeat. Return the list.
pitfalls: Writing a single number as "5..5". A range of one number is written as just the number.
Forgetting the last range when you only emit ranges on a break inside the loop.

Checking for a gap with nums[j + 1] − nums[j] != 1 in a language with 32-bit ints: 2147483647 − (−2147483648) overflows. Compare nums[j + 1] == nums[j] + 1 using a wider type, or rely on JavaScript and Python numbers.

solutions.title: Two pointers over each run
solutions.idea: Start a range at i, extend j while the next value is exactly one more, then write the range and jump to j + 1.

followups: Numbers now arrive one at a time in any order, and you must report the current ranges after each one. What structure keeps that fast?
Go the other way: given a string like "1..4,7,9..10", expand it back into the list of numbers. Which inputs must you reject?
